notes: INCOMPLETE SEARCH. None of the seven required web searches ran: the shared web search budget for the session was used up, and every query was refused. What was checked instead, by opening pages directly: (1) hern.house.gov press release list, pages 1 to 5 (about 45 releases from 20 January 2025 to 22 July 2026): no title or visible excerpt mentions AI; only the two defense bill releases were opened in full, and neither mentions AI; the other releases were judged from titles and truncated excerpts only. (2) hern.house.gov issue list: seven issues, none about AI or technology. (3) Campaign site hernforsenate.com (home page, 'Promises Kept', 'Meet Kevin'): no mention of AI. (4) Public Radio Tulsa site search for 'Hern artificial intelligence': first page of results showed nothing linking Hern to AI; later pages not checked. Pages that could not be opened: hern.house.gov site search (403 error), congress.gov member page (403), govtrack.us member page (403), Oklahoma Voice search (403), NonDoc search (403), KOSU search (403), kevinhern.com (connection reset), News On 6 search (page fetch rate-limited). Because congress.gov and govtrack could not be opened, his bill sponsorships and co-sponsorships on AI were NOT checked. The 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging AI talks with China and the 'Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act' (September 2026): no source was found or opened showing whether Hern signed or co-sponsored; neither was checked against a signatory or co-sponsor list. (He was a House member, not a senator, in September 2026, so signing a senators' letter would be unexpected, but this is an inference, not a verified fact.) Hearing remarks, floor speeches, interviews and op-eds were not searched. Recommend re-running the web searches when the search budget is available before treating 'none' as final. Searches rerun on 15 November 2026: 9 ran, none refused; 0 new statements. Notes from the rerun: All nine searches ran; none were refused. The seven searches marked NOT RUN in the existing file returned nothing linking Hern to superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, AI safety, a pause or slowdown, or AI talks with China. (1) Paraphrase left out: a Bartlesville Radio article from May 2026, 'Hern talks Senate bid while in Bartlesville' (https://bartlesvilleradio.com/pages/news/496362026/hern-talks-senate-bid-while-in-bartlesville), was summarised by the search tool as saying Hern discussed technology and artificial intelligence and that AI will continue increasing productivity in business and daily life. This is a paraphrase from the search summary, not a quote, and the page could not be opened (HTTP 429, rate limited). Even if quoted, it would be level D (promoting AI). A reviewer may want to open that page to check for a direct quote. (2) Off-topic: the hern.house.gov search summary mentioned a Griffin Media interview in which Hern said 'If you go back and just do a little bit of AI, Google or whatever you want to do, you'll see that all of those have been a fallacy', about Affordable Care Act promises. This uses AI only as a way to look things up, so it is off-topic; the page and date were not opened or checked. (3) Opened hern.house.gov DocumentID=4118, a 17 July 2025 op-ed by Hern and Mike Flood on digital assets: it does not mention AI. (4) Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found shows Hern co-sponsoring it; reported co-sponsors were Democrats plus, per one secondhand report, Reps. Whitesides and Moran. Not verified against congress.gov. (5) The 23 September 2026 senators' letter: Hern is not on the verified signer list in the addendum, so he did not sign. (6) Campaign money, not a statement: the Transformer AI campaign finance tracker (https://elections.transformernews.ai/races/ok-s) reportedly lists Defending Our Values PAC (labelled pro-safety) spending about $808,341 supporting Hern and American Mission (labelled pro-innovation) about $252,902; seen only in a search summary, not opened, and not relevant to the grade. Hearing remarks and floor speeches were covered only to the extent these general web searches would surface them; congress.gov was not checked.
